detail: tactic-consolidation-operation Unit 2's Shim-parity check states the criterion "the deriver's item count is >= the raw grep's match count for `decision: deferred`" (and the plan's own top-level Verification fence repeats the same raw-grep comparison). Measured 2026-09-02 against origin state at implementation time: deferredQueue() items=10, raw `grep -rho "decision: deferred" intentions/ | wc -l`=32, defects=48. The 32 decomposes as: 9 self-referential prose quotes of the shim command itself (7 in tactic-consolidation-operation.md's own body describing/testing the shim it defines, 1 in strategy-graph-native-dispatch.md quoting ruling (1) verbatim, 1 in tactic-migration-frontier-projection.md quoting the interim-surface command) — none are wrapped in the `(decision:` parenthetical shape at all, so they are not stamp-shaped; ~5 documentation placeholder examples using literal `YYYY-MM-DD` or describing another node's stamp (tactic-rsi-graph-review.md, tactic-node-review-skill.md, tactic-keystone-decomposition-reorg.md, tactic-substantiation-edge-migration.md, tactic-intent-orchestration-layer-schema.md x2 quoting kind-kind.md's stamp) — these ARE `(decision:` shaped but fail the date/state grammar by construction, since they are documentation, not live dispositions; several malformed-but-real free-prose dispositions (e.g. kind-kind.md's "deferred - Claude-drafted, held for author review", strategy-graph-native-dispatch.md's "deferred - executor decisions held for author review; migrated from ...") that Unit 1's already-committed, already-tested strict tag grammar correctly refuses per its own REFUSE-DONT-SKIP contract — loosening that grammar is out of Unit 2's authority; and stamps recorded in fields outside Unit 2's declared scan scope (node.clarifications[].answer and the node body only). The substitute criterion now encoded in packages/intentionsutil/test/consolidation.test.ts's shim-parity test: over the declared scan scope, enumerate every `(decision: ...)` stamp-shaped span (the same finder parseTolerant uses), classify each as either parsing to state deferred or landing in defects while its own text mentions "deferred", sum that as the honest baseline, and assert items.length + (defects mentioning deferred).length >= baseline, plus a hard floor items.length >= 10 (today's hand-verified count) so a future silent under-collection regression still fails loudly. This directly measures the failure the plan actually feared (a real deferred stamp vanishing with neither an item nor a defect), rather than comparing against a raw-grep baseline the same measurement shows is inflated by prose that merely mentions the shim command. Additional scope finding, separate from the parity criterion: real deferred dispositions exist OUTSIDE Unit 2's declared clarifications+body scan scope — in `rationale` (tactic-align-audit-retirement.md, a `(decision: deferred, delegation-anthropic-claude, 2026-08-30)` stamp inside the frontmatter `rationale:` field) and in nested `attributes.adopted[]` list entries (tradition-hacker-culture.md, tradition-motivation-psychology.md, virtue-knowledge-as-gift.md, each carrying a `(decision: deferred, ...)` stamp inside `attributes.adopted`/`attributes.diverged` prose, not clarifications or body) — these are real, well-formed, parseable stamps deferredQueue cannot see today because Unit 2 declared only two sources. Widening scope to rationale and/or attributes.* is a legitimate future extension but is deliberately NOT made here (coordinator ruling 2026-09-02: do not chase parity by widening scope or loosening Unit 1's grammar). Finally: the plan node's own top-level Verification fence (the raw-grep comparison shell one-liner) is falsified by this same 2026-09-02 measurement and owes an author-side amendment to match the substitute criterion above, or an explicit author ratification that the raw-grep comparison is retired in favor of it. Marked executor-derived, held at deferred authority pending author ratification — Claude found and substituted this criterion during Unit 2 implementation; it has not been reviewed by the author.
